site_or_subject: GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance (2015) and its revision: dual reporting, Scope 2 Quality Criteria, hourly matching and deliverability proposals
operator: GHG Protocol (WRI / WBCSD); Independent Standards Board (ISB); Scope 2 Technical Working Group
record: The GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance (2015) states that "companies shall report scope 2 according to a location-based method and a market-based method" (Executive Summary, s.5.1); the full Guidance (s.3.2, p.11) applies this to operations in "markets with choice in electricity product or supplier". All contractual instruments used in the market-based method "shall" meet the Scope 2 Quality Criteria, among them: "Be tracked and redeemed, retired, or canceled by or on behalf of the reporting entity", "Be issued and redeemed as close as possible to the period of energy consumption", and "Be sourced from the same market in which the reporting entity's electricity-consuming operations are located" (Executive Summary, Table 1, p.6). A Scope 2 Technical Working Group of 45 experts was convened from September 2024. The public consultation on proposed revisions opened on 20 October 2025, was scheduled to close on 19 December 2025, and was "extended to January 31, 2026". The GHG Protocol release named "a new hourly matching and deliverability requirement for market-based reporting" as "a central feature of the proposal", together with load profiles, exemption thresholds, a phased timeline and "a legacy clause for existing contractual commitments"; the consultation slides also proposed using "the most precise location-based emission factor accessible". The feedback summary of 29 July 2026 reports "nearly 1100 responses from 56 countries" and states that "The proposals for hourly matching and deliverability showed low levels of support", while feasibility measures and a legacy clause for existing long-term contracts "received broad support". In July 2026, "ISB members indicated majority support for the idea of developing two marketbased methods": Method 1 would "incorporate hourly matching, deliverability and incrementality" requirements and Method 2 would "maintain existing scope 2 requirements from the 2015 Scope 2 Guidance". The proposed direction is that companies "should report using Method 1 until a to-be-determined date" and "may report using Method 2"; after that date they "shall report using Method 1 if data that meets the quality criteria is available". As of the GHG Protocol update dated 16 October 2026, the revision is not final: a "consolidated public consultation" is "slated for Q2 2027" and the joint GHG Protocol-ISO Corporate Standard is "slated for publication in Q4 2028". No effective date has been published; the 2015 Guidance remains the operative text.

site_or_subject: Mandatory disclosure rules on Scope 2: EU ESRS E1, ISSB IFRS S2, California SB 253, US SEC climate rule
operator: European Commission / EFRAG; ISSB (IFRS Foundation); California Air Resources Board (CARB); US Securities and Exchange Commission
record: EU ESRS E1 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772): EFRAG's Q&A (ID 831, 31 October 2024) cites E1 AR 45(d), which requires undertakings to "apply the location-based and market-based methods to calculate Scope 2 GHG emissions"; the text of E1-6 paragraph 49 itself was not reached. EFRAG's July 2025 draft amended E1 (v1.6, an unapproved working document) keeps paragraph 32(b): "Scope 2 GHG emissions (location-based and market-based)". The European Commission adopted the delegated act on revised ESRS on 3 July 2026 (per EY); EFRAG states the revised standards "will apply to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027", subject to Parliament and Council scrutiny; the adopted revised E1 text was not read. ISSB IFRS S2: paragraph 29(a)(v), as reproduced in an AASB staff paper (21 May 2024), requires an entity to "disclose its location-based Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions" and "provide information about any contractual instruments that is necessary to inform users' understanding"; B31 says the entity "might disclose information about its market-based Scope 2". The ISSB's December 2025 amendments (effective for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027) changed 29(a)(ii), Category 15, GWP and industry-classification rules; 29(a)(v) was not amended. California SB 253: CARB approved the Initial Regulation at its February 2026 meeting, setting a first deadline of 10 August 2026 for a report that "will include only Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions" for entities with "more than $1 billion in annual revenue"; CARB's program page now states the deadline "is November 10, 2026", with the regulation applying "if approved by the Office of Administrative Law". CARB pages read do not state the Scope 2 method; a law-firm summary of CARB's 21 July 2026 workshop reports a proposal that Scope 2 be "calculated and reported using both market-based and location-based methods" under "the current 2015 version of the Scope 2 Guidance", with limited assurance from 2027. US SEC: the March 2024 climate rules were stayed on 4 April 2024; the Eighth Circuit held the challenges in abeyance on 12 September 2025; on 29 May 2026 the SEC proposed "to rescind the climate disclosure rules in their entirety" (Release No. 33-11421). No final rescission was found as of 23 October 2026.

site_or_subject: SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0: Scope 2 target basis and market-based instrument criteria
record: The SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard Version 2.0 was released on 11 June 2026, with an effective date of 1 February 2027 (version history); earlier consultation drafts were published in March 2025 and November 2025. Criterion CNZS-C9.4 states that companies "shall determine target ambition based on the physical GHG inventory, including the location-based method for scope 2". Near-term Scope 2 targets may be absolute reduction targets or low-carbon electricity (LCE) alignment targets "to increase the percentage of LCE used, contracted, or matched on a linear trajectory" (C12.2.a). On instruments, the Standard states "Contracts for plants up to 15 years of age are allowed" and "Existing contracts will be grandfathered for the duration of the contract" (A.5, p.9); activity pools are "defined on the basis of deliverability regions"; a PPA may cover load across pools in one synchronous grid where "the offtake begins within 36 months of the project's commissioning" (C30.3.b); default-delivered LCE counts where "LCE accounts for at least 95% of the generation mix" (C31.1). Hourly matching is not required for target progress: SBTi describes an annual requirement with matching "within a maximum 12-month period", and companies with significant consumption are "required to report the share of electricity consumption matched with low-carbon electricity on an hourly basis". The criteria document sets hourly reporting for pools of 10 GWh or more (C32.1) and voluntary hourly-matching recognition thresholds of 50% to 2030, 75% to 2035 and 90% from 2035 (C34.1). SBTi says exceptions guidance will be "published by Q4 2026" and that it "intends to launch a Call for Evidence on hourly matching".

site_or_subject: Which Scope 2 figure ESG raters and disclosure platforms use: MSCI, Sustainalytics, CDP, S&P Global CSA
operator: MSCI ESG Research; Morningstar Sustainalytics; CDP; S&P Global
record: Sustainalytics' Carbon Emissions Research FAQ (February 2024) states its "Scope 2 data collection is based on the location-based approach since it is more commonly used", and that where a company does not report location-based data "the market-based data are collected instead"; it also states "38% of Scope 1 and 2 is estimated". Its backgrounder states that the ESG Risk Rating assesses carbon through "the carbon own operations material ESG issue (MEI)", covering "own operational energy use and GHG emissions (Scope 1 and 2)". CDP's technical note Accounting of Scope 2 emissions (v12.0, 20 April 2026) states "Companies must report both location-based and market-based scope 2 emissions if they have any" (question 7.7), accepts energy attribute certificates and contracts that meet the GHG Protocol Quality Criteria, answers "Yes" to Guarantees of Origin, RECs and I-RECs counting toward a market-based target, "recommends a vintage limitation of six months before the start of the reporting period", and notes market boundaries "describe, almost universally, national borders". CDP's Full Corporate Scoring Introduction (2024, v1.0) does not describe Scope 2 scoring. MSCI's Greenhouse Gas Emissions Methodologies (June 2024) states that MSCI "collects carbon emissions data (Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3)" and that "Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon emissions are separately estimated" when not reported; neither it, the MSCI ESG Climate Change Metrics methodology (October 2023) nor MSCI's Climate Change Targets FAQ (June 2022) states whether MSCI uses the location-based or market-based Scope 2 figure: not found.
